root_cause.text: The handler iwl_mvm_nd_match_info_handler() lacked a length validation for the variable-length matches array in the notification, so a truncated packet could cause an out-of-bounds read when copying match data via memcpy.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (len < sizeof(struct iwl_scan_offload_match_info))` to `if (len < sizeof(struct iwl_scan_offload_match_info) + matches_len)`, and the commit description states the memcpy assumes the dynamic array `notif->matches` is at least as large as the bytes to copy, and the fix extends validation to ensure sufficient packet length.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `if (len < sizeof(struct iwl_scan_offload_match_info))` to `if (len < sizeof(struct iwl_scan_offload_match_info) + matches_len)`, and the commit description states the memcpy assumes the dynamic array `notif->matches` is at least as large as the bytes to copy, and the fix extends validation to ensure sufficient packet length.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix insufficient length check in scan match info handler to ensure buffer includes variable-length match data.
intent_record.what: Changed the length check condition from comparing against only the size of the fixed struct to also including matches_len, ensuring the buffer is large enough for both the base struct and the variable-length match data.
intent_record.how: This prevents potential out-of-bounds access when parsing the notification's variable-length payload by validating that the provided buffer length is at least sizeof(struct iwl_scan_offload_match_info) + matches_len before proceeding.

grouping_result.intent: Fix insufficient length check in scan match info handler to ensure buffer includes variable-length match data.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the missing length validation for the variable-length matches array in the iwl_mvm_nd_match_info_handler, which is the exact root cause of the out-of-bounds read vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This condition only validates that the buffer length is at least the size of the fixed part of the notification structure, but does not account for the variable-length matches array that follows. A truncated packet with len exactly equal to this size bypasses the check, leading to an out-of-bounds read when later copying match data via memcpy.
